ALONGWITH Case :- FIRST APPEAL No. - 119 of 1982 Appellant :- The State Of U.P.

Respondent :- Panna Lal And 2 Others Counsel for Appellant :- C.S.C.
Counsel for Respondent :- J.B.Dubey Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.
Heard Shri G.K. Pathak, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the appellant-State.
This batch of four appeals preferred by the State assailing the order for grant of compensation in land acquisition matter along with interest @ 6% per annum.

The record would indicate that four other appeals bearing First Appeal No.122 of 1982, First Appeal No.123 of 1982, First Appeal No.125 of 1982 and First Appeal No.127 of 1982 also raised similar grounds upon which the said award passed by the Tribunal was assailed.
The aforesaid four appeals decided as mentioned above are also listed along with the present batch of appeals.

In light of the issue decided in First Appeal No.123 of 1982 against which no further action has been taken and the order passed by this Court dated 10.02.2009 has become final, accordingly, the present appeals being covered by the same judgment as the same issue regarding the award of compensation has been urged in the instant appeals has been decided.

The order dated 10.02.2009 reads as under:-
"This appeal has been filed by the State against the judgment passed by the Reference Court which the compensation was awarded at the rate of Rs.1/- per square feet and the solatium at the rate of 15%and the interest at the rate of 6% per annum from 17.03.1965.
The appeal was filed in the year 1982.

The contention raised by the learned standing counsel is that the claimants are not entitled to get the interest from The State Of U.P. vs Ram Sewak on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/131022225/

sentences.text: The interest is payable from the date of possession of the property.
It has been brought to the notice of the Court that possession of the land was taken by the State on 30.12.1971.
The appeal was admitted.
Notices were issued but nobody appeared on behalf of the respondent.
As there was no interim order, therefore, it appears that claimed amount of claimants must have been paid to the claimants.
It has been argued on behalf of the appellant that the amount of interest granted from 17.03.1965 at the rate of 6% is not correct.
As the possession of the land which was acquired, was taken in the year 1971, therefore, the interest will not be payable from 1965.
I have considered the finding recorded by the court below.

A finding to this effect has been recorded that Section 4 Notification was issued in the month of March, 1962 before the commencement of the Land Acquisition Ordinance, 1967, as such, the interest will be taken to run after the expiry of 3 years from the date of publication of such Notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act.

The Reference Court has taken into consideration Section 367 of the Nagar Maha Palika Adhinium which had modified the Land Acquisition Act for the purposes of acquisition of the land for Nagar Maha Palikas.

Schedule II deals the modification and Section 2 provides that Notification under Section 357 of the Act shall be substituted for and have the same effect as publication of a Notification under Sub-section 1 of Section 4 of the Act.

Therefore, that will have the same effect, under Section 4 and, therefore, after the amendment of Section 6 of the Land Acquisition Act is incorporated by Act No.13 of 1967 along with Section 367 of the Nagar Maha Palika Adhinium and according to Schedule II, the interest will start from the expiry of 3 years from the date of Notification and not from the date of possession.
A finding has also been recorded that State can not delay the payment of interest by merely obtaining possession of the land as and when desired.
Taking into consideration this fact, the Reference Court has granted 6% per annum interest from 17.03.1965 as admittedly the Notification is of 1962.
In view of the aforesaid fact, the contention of the Standing counsel-appellant can not be accepted.
The appeal is devoid of merits and it is hereby dismissed.
No order as to costs."
In view of the aforesaid, the instant appeals are also dismissed.
Consigned to record.

Order Date :- 20.3.2023 Rakesh/-
